L_par_hdr_ssvh.why: Solidity always writes sequencerSetVerifyHash = bytes32(0); Go copies the struct field. Whether Go producers ever set a nonzero value is an intent question, not a codec defect: batch_cache.go:1447-1462 (sealBatch) rejects nonzero sequencerSetVerifyHash for live batches; nonzero is allowed only for legacy replay at index <= legacyCutoverBatchIndex.

L_disch_nonowner.why: After a challenger win, revertReqIndex blocks every non-owner transition until owner revertBatch (replayed). Owner-gated by design; liveness depends on the owner.

L_nat_delay_frontier.why: The delay guard reads the finalized frontier (pendingQueueIndex); 'l1msg delay' fires although all messages are committed, and permissionless finalizeBatch lifts it (replayed). A delay, not a freeze.

L_undo_commit_revert.why: revertBatch leaves batchBlobVersionedHashes/batchDataStore/committedStateRoots (replayed on real Rollup). commitState exists as the designed blob-less recommit path, so the residue looks intentional.

L_undo_enabled.why: commitBatch reverts 'commitBatch requires no stored blob hash' after a revert; commitState succeeds (replayed). Designed recommit path.
